newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Key Hungary shrs weaken, pull index lower.
newsitem.headline: Key Hungary shrs weaken, pull index lower.

text.p: Most leading stocks closed lower on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Wednesday, matching the trend on major European and on central European bourses, traders said.
The BUX index closed at 3,531.54 points, down 40.06.
"This can be regarded a correction as the market firmed recently, but there are many who expect a much bigger correction," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.
"With a few exceptions like Human which strengthened near the end of the session, prices mostly fell," Keresztesi said.
Human, continuing its recent rise, peaked at a new high of 2,610 forints, although by close it fell to 2,595, up 195 over yesterday.
"Some say that Human was in the shadow of other pharmaceuticals and now tries to make up for it," she said.
The fact alone that Human's price is well below that of Richter and Egis, the two other drugs shares on the market, does not explain the rise, Keresztesi added.

Ciba-Geigy AG's Hungarian unit and Humanpharma, member of the Human group, announced today that they will boost their cooperation in Hungary as Ciba will have its two most important products manufactured here for the Hungarian market.

Keresztesi said she regarded Richter's fall the most surprising today. In active trade Richter fell to a daily low of 8,000 forints from where it rebounded to end at 8,350 forints, 250 forints below its close on Tuesday.

Textile producer company Pannon-Flax firmed five forints to end at 405 in only one deal, after it announced that it will continue talks to buy the assets of the Lorinci spinning plant of Masterfil Rt.
BUX index futures ended lower for all maturities, by 35.00 to 70.00 points except for December 1997, which remained unchanged at 4,200 points.
